bottom_line: In men with chronic congestive heart failure on digoxin and a diuretic, hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate vs placebo reduced cumulative mortality at two years (25.6 percent vs 34.3 percent; risk reduction 34 percent, P<0.028).
implications: These results support a lower cumulative mortality with hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate vs placebo through two years (25.6 percent vs 34.3 percent) with an adjusted Cox-model mortality-risk reduction estimate of 34 percent (P<0.028; 95 percent confidence interval, 4 to 54 percent), while prazosin showed no difference vs placebo. The document also notes that beyond three years the study had insufficient data for comparison and that full-dose persistence with hydralazine–isosorbide was limited (55 percent at six months).

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized trial in 642 men on digoxin and a diuretic, assigned to placebo, prazosin, or hydralazine plus isosorbide dinitrate.
major_points.quote: we randomly assigned 642 men with impaired car- diac function and reduced exercise tolerance who were taking digoxin and a diuretic to receive additional double- blind treatment with placebo, prazosin (20 mg per day), or the combination of hydralazine

major_points.text: Average follow-up was 2.3 years (range 6 months to 5.7 years).
major_points.quote: Follow-up averaged 2.3 years (range, 6 months to 5.7 years).

major_points.text: Cox model estimate for first two years: 34% reduction in mortality risk with hydralazine–nitrate vs placebo (P<0.028; 95% CI 4 to 54 percent).
major_points.quote:
For the first two-
year period, the Cox life-table regression model yield-
ed an estimate of a cumulative reduction in mortality
risk of 34 percent in the hydralazine-nitrate group, as
compared with the placebo group (P<0.028; 95 per-
cent confidence interval, 4 to 54 percent).

major_points.text: Prazosin had no mortality difference vs placebo.
major_points.quote:
Life-table analysis that was based on intention to
treat and that included all deaths revealed no dif-
ference between the prazosin and placebo groups

major_points.text: Side effects led to discontinuation; only 55% were taking full doses of both hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate at 6 months.
major_points.quote:
Only 55 percent were taking full doses of both drugs
six months after randomization.

criticisms.text: Not possible to define the relative roles of hydralazine vs isosorbide dinitrate because they were used in combination.
criticisms.quote:
Since both hydralazine, an arteriolar dilator,”° and
isosorbide dinitrate, predominantly a venous dila-
tor,?” were used in combination in the present trial,
it is not possible to define the relative roles of the
two agents.
